title: Modular Schur numbers: S_m(k,ℓ) = n − 1 for k ≥ n − 1, where n = m/gcd(m,ℓ−1)
abstract: A Lean 4 formalization, with Mathlib, of the main results of the paper "Prime-power structure of the stable regime for modular Schur numbers" (docs/paper/modular-schur.pdf in this repository). The modular Schur number S_m(k,ℓ), introduced by Chappelon, Revuelta Marchena and Sanz Domínguez (2013), is the largest N such that 1, …, N can be coloured with k colours so that no colour class contains a solution of x_1 + ⋯ + x_ℓ ≡ y (mod m). For m ≥ 2 and ℓ ≥ 2, put n = m/gcd(m,ℓ−1). The main theorem is the closed form S_m(k,ℓ) = n − 1 for every k ≥ n − 1. D'orville, Sim, Wong and Ho (Integers 25 (2025) #A62) gave it when gcd(m,ℓ−1) = 1 (their Corollary 5). The general case is a short corollary of the singleton criterion and their Corollary 3; to the author's knowledge it is first stated in the paper. The proof turns on one value: ℓ copies of n sum to n modulo m, so the class {n} alone breaks the rule, while each of 1, …, n − 1 is safe in a class of its own. The formalization also proves the one-colour closed form S_m(1,ℓ) = min(ℓ − 1, ⌊m/ℓ⌋) for 2 ≤ ℓ ≤ m, which answers Problem 1.3 of D'orville et al.; the bound S_m(k,ℓ) ≤ m − 1 of Chappelon et al.; and the reduction from integers to residues modulo m. Twelve theorems with Mathlib-only statements are compared by lake comparator (statement identity, permitted axioms, and replay through the Lean, nanoda and con-ron kernels); their only axioms are propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The 33 project modules also contain further results, listed in LEAN_STATUS.md, that are proved and axiom-audited but are not compared, among them the bound m/p, with p the least prime factor of m, on the size of a set of residues whose pairwise differences all lie in a proper subgroup of ℤ/m. An earlier computational part of the project, which uses native_decide, is not in this repository and is not part of these results. The informal proofs, the Lean formalization and the paper were produced with AI systems (Claude, Aristotle and GPT-5) under the direction of the author.
